name: Centro (Main Plaza / Zocalo)
description: The village center around the main plaza is where island life concentrates: colorful street art, ice cream stands, taco carts, small markets, and most guesthouses. It's the walkable core most visitors base themselves in, close to golf cart rentals, restaurants, and the short path to the main beach.
bestFor: First-time visitors, budget stays, walkable convenience
cons: Can get crowded and noisy in high season
Sandy streets get muddy after rain

name: Punta Cocos (East End)
description: East of the village toward the small airstrip, this stretch has a quieter, more resort-like feel with boutique hotels and cabanas fronting calmer water. It's a short golf cart or bike ride from the center, offering more space and privacy while still reachable for dinners in town.
pros: Still a short ride to town amenities
cons: Requires a golf cart or bike for daily errands

name: Punta Mosquito (West End)
description: The western tip of the island is a wilder, largely undeveloped area known for flamingo sightings, shallow sandbars stretching into the sea, and mangrove-lined shoreline. It's more of a day-trip destination than a place to stay, reached by golf cart, bike, or boat tour along unpaved tracks.
cons: Little to no infrastructure or shade
Access can be rough, especially after rain

name: Ferry Harbour Area
description: The harbour where ferries from Chiquila dock sits at the edge of the village, lined with golf cart taxi stands, small shops, and a few restaurants catering to arriving and departing travelers. It's a functional, transit-oriented pocket rather than a destination, but useful for early departures or late arrivals.
bestFor: Early ferry departures, short layovers, transit convenience
pros: A few solid casual eateries nearby
cons: Less scenic and more utilitarian than the rest of town
Can feel congested when ferries arrive
